notes.A26: The arched opening and radiating tunnel surround match the neutral stem; the warning does not itself supply additional tunnel operating rules.
notes.A27: The tilted car and broken edge match weak/high road edge, with margin advice rather than invented priority.
notes.A28: The black diagonal cross is a right-hand-rule junction warning, distinct from oncoming priority and zone-end alternatives.
notes.A29: The broad vertical road and thin lateral branches match the selected junction; joining traffic yields/stops, without removing care duties.
notes.A30: Three circulating arrows in a warning triangle anticipate a roundabout; they are distinct from compulsory-roundabout blue-circle instructions.
notes.A31: The tractor/trailer faces left and represents slow traffic crossing/entering, not a compulsory slow-vehicle route.
notes.A32: The visible horse/cart is one animal-drawn variant; the meaning is not narrowed to horses despite the specific neutral picture.
notes.A33: Tracked snowmobile with front skis matches off-road scooter traffic, avoiding an ordinary moped interpretation.
notes.A34: The overlapping cars warn of queue formation, without asserting that a queue is already present.
notes.A35: The barrier/fence symbol denotes a railway or tram crossing fitted with barriers; controls still govern passage.
notes.A36: The steam locomotive belongs to the barrier-free railway warning; absence of a barrier is not evidence of no train.
notes.A37: The tram with overhead diamond identifies the barrier-free tram crossing, not a roundabout or direction sign.
notes.A38: Three red stripes are the first third-based approach marker; no universal metre distance is inferred.
notes.A39: The single crossbuck and central track depiction agree with the exact source artwork; one/multiple-track arrangements are not interchanged.
notes.A40: The actual rounded vertical bar is accurately described without inventing a separate dot; meaning requires supplementary hazard information.
notes.A41: The sideways car depicts accident warning, without implying an exact restriction or guaranteed traffic state.
notes.B1: Inverted triangle is give-way; the T2/T3 advance-information qualification is retained rather than applying immediate stopping everywhere.
notes.B2: STOP lettering and red octagon support a complete stop; stop-line and default-position rules are not confused with mere yielding.
notes.B3: Pedestrian over stripes in the blue square identifies the crossing; the yielding sentence explicitly scopes itself to uncontrolled crossings.
notes.B4: The yellow diamond denotes priority-road designation, not permission to ignore actual controls or hazards.
notes.B5: The diagonal band ends the priority-road designation; later junction priority must be assessed anew.
notes.B6: Red upward and black downward arrows correctly put the yielding duty on the viewer's direction, unlike B7.
notes.B7: White upward/red downward arrows put the duty on oncoming traffic but do not justify forcing passage.
notes.B8: The cyclist/stripes blue sign is a cycle crossing, with driver and rider duties preserved; it is not merely a cycle passage marking.
notes.C1: The red circle/yellow bar prohibits entry from this direction; it is not the two-way traffic prohibition.
